### New

- **A switch made from the menu bar now shows that it is working.** The menu closes on the
  click and nothing follows the switch, so a slow one — a host that is asleep, or one being
  waited on — looked exactly like nothing having happened. People clicked again, and the
  second click queued a second switch against a display the first was still on. The menu now
  carries the state itself: its heading reads "Switching to &lt;host&gt;…" and every host in
  it, including the ones in each display's submenu, is unclickable. A repeat click is dropped
  rather than queued.
- **A switch still running after 1.2 seconds opens a small panel** naming the host it is
  switching to. Most switches finish well inside that, and a panel that flashes up and away
  is worse than none, which is what the threshold is for. The panel closes itself when the
  switch lands.
- **A switch that fails stays in that panel.** A failure from the menu bar used to reach the
  log and nothing else — the screen said nothing at all. The panel now names the display that
  would not switch and why, one line per display. Got it, Enter or Esc dismisses it.

### Fixes

- **The menu bar toolbar's icons did not land on the pixel grid.** The tallest box in the row
  is the page tabs, which inherited the 1.45 line-height ratio and came out 40.84375px tall at
  13px. Centring anything in a fractional row lands it on a fraction: the two round buttons sat
  at y=17.421875 and their glyphs at 25.921875, which is 51.84 device pixels at 2x. On top of
  that, a 17px glyph in a 34px button leaves 8.5px of margin — measured in the app, the ink sat
  0.5px right of and below the circle's middle, at every rotation angle. Standing still it read
  as softness; once the refresh icon spun it was obvious. The row's line heights are pixels now
  and the glyphs are an even size, which measures 0.00.
- **The status pill's contents sat left of centre.** A label ending in a full-width closing
  bracket — "Network Agent not configured (DDC unaffected)" in Traditional Chinese — left 12px
  of air on the left and 22.5px on the right. Full-width closing punctuation is drawn in the
  left half of its em and advances the empty other half anyway. That half em is given back, as
  CJK typesetting does at the end of a line.

This release speaks the same protocol as v0.8.0 and pairs and switches with it.

### Known limits

- The 1.2-second threshold is fixed and not yet a setting.
- The macOS DMG is ad-hoc signed and not yet notarized with an Apple Developer ID, so
  Gatekeeper may ask for it to be allowed by hand.
